## Computing Environment of the Replicator

# Replication

- Downloaded code and data from dropbox.
- Commited code to git repo.
- Ran Section I (`Rscript code/run_all.R`) as per README. The code ran to completion successfully without errors and compiled `paper.pdf` containing all 47 exhibits.
- Ran Section II (`Rscript code/run_simulated.R`) as per README.
- Initial run failed during compilation due to missing CmdStan and other packages (`cmdstanr`, `doParallel`, `foreach`, `data.table`, `tictoc`, `MASS`, `fixest`).
- Installed required packages manually. 
- Code ran to completion and generated `paper_simulated.pdf`. 

# Findings {#sec-findings}

The replication reproduced the overall structure of the paper and the qualitative results in the tables and figures, including consistency between data and model outputs across panels. All numbers and exhibits from Section I successfully match the original paper exactly, since they are generated from precomputed intermediates.

Section II successfully runs end-to-end using simulated data, and differences in the levels of the plotted values and tables were observed (e.g., in the Appendices), but these were expected since simulated data generates qualitatively similar but numerically different results.

## Data Preparation Code

- Program `run_all.R` ran without error, output expected data.
- Program `run_simulated.R` ran successfully after missing dependencies were installed.

## Tables and Figures

All figures and tables in the main text of the paper were successfully generated by `run_all.R`. Simulated outputs from `run_simulated.R` were also successfully produced.


When running Section I (`run_all.R`) with the precomputed intermediates derived from the proprietary data, all tables and figures perfectly match the original paper numerically and visually. 
When running Section II (`run_simulated.R`), all 41 code-generated tables and figures (every table in the paper and every figure except the 6 static photographs) are numerically different from the original paper. This is expected because they are generated using synthetic data. As noted by the authors, they are qualitatively similar, though demand frictions are somewhat lower in the simulated model, leading to smaller counterfactual welfare gains and different optimal pricing lever magnitudes. The "Reproduced?" column below reflects the exact reproduction using Section I.

## Other Issues

- A `LICENSE.txt` file is provided with the MIT License for the "replication package". However, the authors do not explicitly specify whether the license applies to both the data and the code, or only the code (the text of the MIT license itself refers only to "software").
- Unzipping the archive creates a nested folder (replication-package/jinvass26_replication_may_19_2016/). Instead, the contents should extract directly into the replication-package directory.
- `paper-appendices` folder provided is empty. Please copy the final paper also to that directory.

## Reason for incomplete reproducibility

- [x] None.
- [ ] `Discrepancy in output` (either figures or numbers in tables or text differ)
- [ ] `Bugs in code` that were fixable by the replicator (but should be fixed in the final deposit)
- [ ] `Code missing`, in particular if it prevented the replicator from completing the reproducibility check
  - [ ] `Data preparation code missing` should be checked if the code missing seems to be data preparation code
- [ ] `Code not functional` is more severe than a simple bug: it prevented the replicator from completing the reproducibility check
- [ ] `Software not available to replicator` may happen for a variety of reasons, but in particular (a) when the software is commercial, and the replicator does not have access to a licensed copy, or (b) the software is open-source, but a specific version required to conduct the reproducibility check is not available.
- [ ] `Insufficient time available to replicator` is applicable when (a) running the code would take weeks or more (b) running the code might take less time if sufficient compute resources were to be brought to bear, but no such resources can be accessed in a timely fashion (c) the replication package is very complex, and following all (manual and scripted) steps would take too long.
- [ ] `Data missing` is marked when data *should* be available, but was erroneously not provided, or is not accessible via the procedures described in the replication package
- [ ] `Data not available` is marked when data requires additional access steps, for instance purchase or application procedure. 
- [ ] `Missing README` is marked if there is no README to guide the replicator, or the README is not in compliance with JPE requirements
